advice:
Own verdict: Sound only as a distinct failure-recovery cohort, not as a way to reach >20 independent sessions; continuing the same failed IDs yields recovery evidence but not new sessions, so the >20 count must come from distinct real sessions and the original deficits must remain visible.
Independent review: I accept preserving exact IDs, receipts/hashes and accepted=false as genuine, non-re-rolled evidence. I reject its allowance that continuation turns can count toward the qualifying-session count—that conflates one session with many and risks masking failure.
Next: log continuations under a separate cohort label; report distinct-session vs. continuation-extended counts separately; verify representative compaction feedback retention and that failed code isn't re-submitted unchanged.
Risk: stop if any continuation is used to claim original acceptance, inflate the independent-session count, or bypass protocol/history bounds.
